title: The cloud presence: a placeholder page with the name, and services only when a plan item needs one
body:
Maintainer, 2026-09-30, first:

> "We'll still need a cloud presence for maybe a static website or something basic, since there's no intention of this becoming an externally-facing project in the near term. This is more just for fun than anything else."

and then, narrowing it:

> "The static page could even be less. It might simply just be the name, and that's it. Since I'm fairly actively not working to get people onboarded (since we're not ready to support other players), we only really need the site to help provide any backend services around updates, etc., or if we want custom runners or any cloud services to help with this."

Register rows D-WORKFLOW-097 and 098. The site is outside 0.0.1 (#344); what follows is the whole of the fork's cloud presence until a plan item shows a need for more.

## What exists today

- The domain `rasteratops.com` is registered at iwantmyname; its mail is on Hostinger; its name servers move from iwantmyname to Cloudflare (D-WORKFLOW-104, 105); no web record, no page.
- The release page and the tracker are `rasteratops/distribution` on GitHub, and nobody is being onboarded: other players are not supported yet.
- #344's P0 read decides whether the updater needs an endpoint at all (Branch A re-points it at the release page; Branch B is manual adoption); no manifest or update service is in 0.0.1.

## Shape

1. **The placeholder.** One page at the domain carrying the name, and nothing else: no install text, no links, no analytics. GitHub Pages from a small repository in the organisation or Hostinger's static hosting, GitHub Pages chosen (D-WORKFLOW-099); the DNS record at Cloudflare (D-WORKFLOW-104).
2. **Services, only on a shown need.** An update endpoint, a hosted or custom runner, or any other cloud service is its own item, opened when a plan item names the need (the P0 updater note; the P5 hosted-QA experiment log), never in advance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A DNS record at Cloudflare points the domain at GitHub Pages, and `curl -sI https://rasteratops.com/` answers `200` with `text/html`; the page's text, stripped of markup, is the name and no more.
- [ ] No other page, link, form, script or tracker is served from the domain: a crawl of the root finds exactly one document.
- [ ] Any cloud service beyond the placeholder is filed as its own issue that cites the plan item needing it, before it is created; none exists otherwise.
- [ ] If the site has a workflow, it runs on hosted runners only, never on the self-hosted runner (#344 P1's trigger rule).

title: The secret store: OpenBao in a container on a small machine of its own (Vultr or Hostinger), off the build host

milestone.title: Infrastructure topology
milestone.description: Acceptance test: the fork runs on infrastructure of its own, provisioned from a secret-free blueprint: the secret store (#347) on a machine of its own, the agent host and its network (#348) on the non-work tailnet with a bastion and an egress box, the backup location chosen and the restore drill completing a warm build on a clean host with no secret present. Each criterion is a drill log, a listing or a tool PASS line.

body:
Maintainer, 2026-09-30, on #344's questions 3 and 4:

> "I'd rather spin up some lightweight infrastructure for this somewhere. We could either continue to build more on Hostinger and put it there, or use Vultr for that."

> "I do think containerizing it would be good if we want to then move it elsewhere."

Register row D-WORKFLOW-103. The plan item that needs it (#345's rule for any cloud service): #344 P1's backup and custody exits, and register rows 10 and 14 of that plan (organisation recovery and 2FA custody; backup scope and the recovery drill). Not on the build host, not on the QA host.

## The choice, with the recommendation

| | Vultr | Hostinger VPS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Already in use | named as the vendor for any cloud box (D-WORKFLOW-084); nothing there yet | the domain and the mail |
| The machine | the smallest always-on instance, a plain VM, snapshots and block storage by the vendor | a VPS plan, a plain VM |
| Billing | a second vendor | one vendor for domain, mail and this |
| Recommendation | **yes**: one vendor for everything that is a machine, and mail and DNS stay where they are | fine if consolidating bills matters more than one machine vendor |

## Shape

- One small VM, joined to the maintainer's tailnet, reachable only over it (no public port for the store); the vendor's firewall closes everything else.
- OpenBao in a container with its data on a mounted volume, so the pair moves as a unit; vendor snapshots of the volume on a schedule, and the restore rehearsed once.
- Unseal material held outside the VM (the maintainer's existing store or password manager), never on serval.
- The bot (blitterbot, on serval today; D-WORKFLOW-136, #374) reads what it needs through a scoped policy; serval holds no recovery material.
- What it holds for 0.0.1: an encrypted copy of the bot's three secrets (the GitHub token, the mail token, the ssh key) and the two owner accounts' recovery codes; the token-expiry reminder is configured on the mail channel.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The provider is named in a comment here and in a register row citing this issue.
- [ ] `tailscale status` on serval lists the store's machine, and a connection to its OpenBao port from outside the tailnet is refused (a `curl` from a non-tailnet address times out or is refused, recorded).
- [ ] `docker inspect` (or the Podman equivalent) on the machine shows the OpenBao container with its data on a mounted volume; a vendor snapshot of that volume exists with its ID recorded, and a restore of it to a fresh VM brings the store up unsealed with the same secrets, recorded once.
- [ ] `bao kv get` (or the API) from serval, under the bot's policy, returns the bot's own secrets and is refused the recovery codes; the policy file is committed.
- [ ] `grep -r` of the recovery material's identifiers on serval finds nothing outside the encrypted copy's absence: the recovery codes exist only in the store.
- [ ] #344 P1's backup exit cites this issue's snapshot ID and restore record.

title: The agent's host and the network: a small machine for blitterbot, everything locked inside a tailnet (Tailscale or Headscale)

milestone.title: Infrastructure topology
milestone.description: Acceptance test: the fork runs on infrastructure of its own, provisioned from a secret-free blueprint: the secret store (#347) on a machine of its own, the agent host and its network (#348) on the non-work tailnet with a bastion and an egress box, the backup location chosen and the restore drill completing a warm build on a clean host with no secret present. Each criterion is a drill log, a listing or a tool PASS line.

body:
Maintainer, 2026-09-30:

> "Related, since we're already looking at a cloud service for OpenBao, we could create another one for the agent, and we could lock this all down inside of a tailnet, or if it's easy enough to do, a headscale. I have less experience with that open source alternative, but I'm certainly open to exploring it if it offers the right functionality."

and, on the provider:

> "I'd rather go with what we think is the best longer term cloud provider. I'd never used Hostinger until yesterday, and so if you'd like to research the two and what would be best for our longer term needs as well between Vulture and Hostinger, let's pick between those two."

This is the bot's host, the second half of D-WORKFLOW-095; the store is #347 and the provider research lands there.

## What exists today

- blitterbot's credentials (the GitHub token, the ssh key, the mail token) sit on serval, the build host, in `~/.config/rasteratops/` and `~/.ssh/`; every `gh` call, commit and mail read runs there.
- The maintainer's machines already share a tailnet (Tailscale, `*.tailad0ff1.ts.net`): serval and marvin at least; the maintainer works from a Mac and reaches serval over ssh.
- #344 P1 wants credential-holding roles apart from build and QA roles, and the runner user unable to read the bot's stores.

## Shape to decide

1. **The bot's host:** a small VM at the same provider as #347's store, or the same VM as the store (one machine, two containers), or an SBC at home. The bot needs: `gh`, git over ssh, the mail SDK, the council Facilitator (Node 24), and a way to run things on serval (ssh over the tailnet); it does not need to build.
2. **The network:** everything (serval, the second Lenovo, the store, the bot's host, the Mac) inside one tailnet with an ACL that lets the bot reach serval and the store and nothing reach the store but the bot and the owner. Tailscale's control plane, or Headscale, the open-source control server that the same Tailscale clients talk to, self-hosted on the store's or the bot's VM. The research on #347 covers what Headscale supports and what it costs to run.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The host and the network are named in a comment here and in a register row citing this issue.
- [ ] `tailscale status` on serval lists the bot's host, and the tailnet's ACL file (committed, secrets-free) allows bot→serval ssh and bot→store, and denies every other peer→store; a denied connection is recorded once.
- [ ] `gh api user --jq .login` run on the bot's host reads `blitterbot`, a signed commit pushed from it reads verified on the API, and the mail reader lists the inbox from there; the same three on serval no longer have the credentials (`test -r` on each path prints `1` for the runner user and the files are absent for the build user).
- [ ] If Headscale: its container runs on the named VM with its data on a mounted volume, every existing device re-registered against it, MagicDNS and the ACL working, and a vendor snapshot of its volume recorded; if Tailscale: the plan's limits (users, devices) are recorded and under the fleet's count.


Identity update, 2026-10-02: D-WORKFLOW-136 / #374 rename the existing account to `blitterbot` (same ID 335883270) and use `blitterbot@rasteratops.com`; dated earlier observations retain their historical names.

## Scope

Finish #344's component/source publication gate for the qualified VM18, H70002 and SM855003 images. #492 owns completed firmware builds and their exact per-image inventory attachment; this task owns remaining licence/source dispositions and publication custody. The M7 milestone body remains the ordered plan.

The five architecture profiles now map 584 VM, 224 H700 ARM, 615 H700 aarch64, 228 SM8550 ARM and 676 SM8550 aarch64 components. These are per-profile rows, not a unique-component total. The original failed inventory attempts remain unchanged; the final record explicitly composes individually successful reports. No firmware changes or new audit are implied.

Seventeen components lack recipe licence declarations: common-shaders, enet, freej2me-lr, glsl-shaders, harfbuzz-icu, libretro-database, libspeexdsp, libxmp-lite, openbor, opusfile, rclone, retropie-shaders, rocknix-abl, slang-shaders, tailscale, wildmidi and zerotier-one. Notice candidates are retained for 47 component/profile rows; absence or presence of a notice is not a licence conclusion.

Special inputs: ARM compatibility components; LLVM's exact pinned source archive and three installed libraries (the SM8550 unpacked root is absent); FEX's Nix toolchains/archives and 81 referenced store paths; recovered, hash-pinned amd64/arm64 rclone ZIPs that match the unpacked binaries; and exact installed Doom shareware bytes from idtech-lr's unpinned install-time URL. Do not classify a package as build-only merely because it lacks its own image install stamp: vendored/static dependencies require disposition too. A prebuilt archive is not corresponding source.

Can this be done on the VM? This is read-only host/artifact/source work; no physical fact, personal cloud or device mutation is needed. Hardware smoke, #519 owner alignment and publication authorization remain separate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every selected image and ARM compatibility profile has a component inventory tied to its immutable bundle and original input-manifest hash, with a source/licence disposition per component, including embedded/vendored dependencies.
- [ ] The 17 missing declarations and special inputs above have source-cited dispositions and retained exact notices; no recipe-header licence is substituted for the shipped third-party work's licence. Any required product change has its own rebuilt/requalified artifact before release.
- [ ] A fork-owned corresponding-source bundle retains exact fetched source archives/git/submodules, fork patches and build scripts, with machine-readable hashes and a complete component-to-member map. Prebuilt rclone/ABL/shareware assets and Nix inputs are explicitly assessed rather than silently counted as source.
- [ ] Independent retrieval and hash verification of the source bundle pass, and the required backup custody is evidenced; local source-cache existence and public repository visibility alone do not close this criterion.
- [ ] #344, M7, the release manifest/notes and canonical checkpoint link the final inventory, bundle and any remaining physical/publication gates. Publication is not claimed while an unresolved disposition remains.

## Current evidence

Prepared repository packet: `docs/qa-logs/2026-10-08-final-inventory/` (publish and bind its commit before closure). Supplement owner `/workspace/tmp/pixelelated-m7-source-supplement-01` completed with all five original rc0 results and actual process cleanup. Older inventory12 is historical and cannot substitute for these images.

The maintained contract is D-WORKFLOW-139 and #344's corresponding-source/component-inventory obligation. This is a concrete implementation child of that existing approved scope, not a new release policy.
